questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Matrices in Row Echelon Form
questions.problem:
Which of the following matrices are **not** in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry ${a}_{43}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry ${c}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $A$ and $C$ are **not** in row echelon form.

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, only $A$ and $C$ are **not** in row echelon form.

questions.problem:
Which of the following matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the second row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Augmented Matrices in Row Echelon Form
questions.problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are **not** in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -4 & 5 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is not in row echelon form since ${a}_{33}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not in row echelon form since the third row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since ${c}_{33}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -4 & 5 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ are **not** in row echelon form.

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ are **not** in row echelon form.
